confidence_explanation: The evidence clearly shows a mid-session IP change for user_10, followed by a rapid sequence of cross-departmental file downloads that fall outside the user's authorized directory baseline, strongly indicating session hijacking and subsequent data exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: User_10 logs in successfully from their normal IP (192.168.1.110) and begins legitimate file reading within authorized directories.
The session (sess_user_10_20260505_001) is hijacked; the source IP changes from the normal 192.168.1.110 to an external IP 91.219.236.222 mid-session.
The attacker begins downloading sensitive files, starting with a finance budget file.
The attacker performs cross-departmental data exfiltration, downloading files from DevOps runbooks, logs, marketing, and engineering directories.
The attacker logs out from the hijacked session.

gaps: Geographic location of the hijacked IP (91.219.236.222) to confirm it is not a known VPN used by the user.
Network logs showing how the session hijacking occurred (e.g., cookie theft or man-in-the-middle).
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred involving user_10. After an initial legitimate login from a known IP, the session was hijacked by an external IP (91.219.236.222), which then proceeded to exfiltrate multiple files from departments outside of the user's authorized scope, including engineering, marketing, and devops.
